successCriteria.description: Exactly one new file exists at `migrations/20260914000001_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js`, is CommonJS, and exports both `up` and `down` as async functions taking `knex` — matching the signature of the two existing migrations. No other file in the repo is added or modified.

After `up` runs, `leave_requests` has a `reverses_request_id` column that is nullable and text-typed (no NOT NULL, no default, no foreign key constraint), and every pre-existing row reads NULL for it — i.e. the addition is backward compatible with rows created before the migration.

After `up` runs, a UNIQUE index named `leave_requests_reverses_request_id_unique` exists on `leave_requests(reverses_request_id)` and is PARTIAL — restricted to rows where `reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`. Verified behaviourally: inserting two rows with NULL `reverses_request_id` succeeds, while inserting a second row with the same non-null `reverses_request_id` is rejected by the database.

`down` reverses `up` completely and in the correct order: the index is dropped before the column, and after `down` the `leave_requests` table has no `reverses_request_id` column and no leftover index of that name. A migrate:latest -> migrate:rollback -> migrate:latest cycle completes without error.

The migration applies cleanly from an empty database on BOTH engines the smoke check uses: `npx knex migrate:latest --env test` (sqlite3) and `--env smoke_pg` (PostgreSQL) both exit 0 with the new migration recorded in `knex_migrations`.

The full verification command stays green with no source changes: `npm run build` (tsc) exits 0, the Jest suite passes, and `npm run smoke` passes — the nullable column is inert because the leave repository's `COLUMNS` list does not yet select it.

constraints: Scope is exactly one file: `migrations/20260914000001_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js`. No TypeScript source, model, repository, service, route, seed, or test file may be created or modified in this phase.

The column must be nullable text with NO foreign key, NO NOT NULL, and NO default. The self-reference to `leave_requests.id` is expressed only by the value convention, not by a DB constraint — portability across pg and sqlite3 is the reason.
The unique index MUST be partial (`WHERE reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`). A plain unique index would collide on the NULLs carried by every original row and break the existing table.
`down` must drop the index before the column, and both steps must be idempotent-safe (`DROP INDEX IF EXISTS`). Dropping the column first would leave a dangling index.

The migration must be portable across pg and sqlite3 — no engine-specific DDL, no `t.uuid`, no `json`/`jsonb`, no `ALTER ... ADD CONSTRAINT`. Both engines must accept the column, the partial unique index, and the drop sequence.
The migration file must be CommonJS (`exports.up` / `exports.down`), not ESM, and its timestamp prefix must sort after `20260913000000` and `20260913000001` so it applies last.
The file must carry a comment documenting the semantics: NULL on an original request, equal to the original's `id` on a reversal row, and a reversal row is terminal (never itself reversed).
No secondary non-unique access-path index on `reverses_request_id` in this phase — only the column and the unique partial index.
outOfScope: Any TypeScript change: `leave.model.ts`, `leave.repository.ts`, `leave.service.ts`, routes, controllers, or the `@trackeros/contracts` surface. The column is inert until Phase 2.
Any test file — no new Jest unit tests, no smoke stage additions. Phase 4 and Phase 5 own those.

A foreign key constraint from `reverses_request_id` to `leave_requests.id`, despite the reconciled architecture prose calling it a self-referencing FK. The task and PLAN.md explicitly forbid it for pg/sqlite3 portability.
The secondary non-unique `reverses_request_id` access-path index mentioned incidentally in the reconciled architecture. Only the unique partial index is in scope.
The reversal business logic itself — the APPROVED branch of `LeaveService.cancel`, balance release, audit record, notification, and terminality rejection. Phase 3 owns it.
Any change to `knexfile.js`, `package.json`, seeds, or the existing two migrations.

entityInvariants.invariant: NULL means the row is an original request; a non-null value equals the `id` of the original request this row reverses. The column is write-once at insert and is never updated — a reversal row is terminal and is never itself reversed.
At most one row may exist per non-null `reverses_request_id`; any number of rows may carry NULL. This is the structural exactly-once guarantee that a completed approval is reversed at most once.
Every row that existed before this migration remains valid and readable with `reverses_request_id` NULL; no existing column, constraint, or index is altered or dropped.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Not applicable — schema DDL, no request context, no RBAC surface.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Both functions are async and must reject/throw on failure so knex aborts the migration and does not record it in `knex_migrations`. `up` must be safe to run against a database where the two prior migrations have already applied. `down` must not throw when the index or column is already absent.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Match the module format, function signature, and leading block-comment convention of the existing migrations exactly — CommonJS `exports.up = async function up(knex)` / `exports.down = async function down(knex)`, with a comment explaining the column's nullability and semantics.

The column type convention must match how the initial schema types `leave_requests.id` and its free-text columns — `t.text(...)`, nullable, string ids rather than native uuid — so the schema stays portable across pg and sqlite3.

The migration must be discovered and applied by the existing knex configuration without any config change: `migrations.directory` is `./migrations` and `tableName` is `knex_migrations` for every env, including the per-run `smoke_pg` schema.

The column name must be exactly `reverses_request_id` (snake_case, matching the table's existing column naming) so the Phase 2 repository `COLUMNS`/`mapRow` mapping to `reversesRequestId` resolves against a real column.
The index name must be exactly `leave_requests_reverses_request_id_unique` so the `down` drop and any later reference resolve to the same object.

integrationPoints.why: The smoke check migrates from empty on sqlite3 or real Postgres; this migration must apply cleanly on both or the whole smoke run fails.
Phase 2 threads this column through the repository. This phase must leave the column inert — the repository's fixed COLUMNS list does not select it yet, so no existing query breaks.

integrationPoints.target: knexfile.js migration config (directory, tableName, smoke_pg searchPath/schemaName)
integrationPoints.why: The file is picked up by the existing config with no change; the per-run smoke schema means the migration must be schema-agnostic (no hardcoded schema qualification).
